title: The same steel rack rig from the rear
blurb: Rear view of the same highway rig: the rack frame fills the back of the trailer, one yellow strap visible along the right side.
photo_credit: Photo: Oregon Department of Transportation, CC BY 2.0 via Wikimedia Commons. QA sweep development run, Oct 26, 2026.

calibration.axis: x (front at bed_min_x, rear at bed_max_x)
calibration.method: pixels-per-inch from the trailer_bed mask bitmap tight extent
calibration.reason: the bed extent is taller than it is wide in this frame, so the side-view x-axis mapping does not apply (photo may be rotated or a top-down view)

measurements.name: rear_overhang
measurements.method: rearmost cargo extent (mask bitmap tight edge, else bbox) minus the bed rear edge, scaled by the calibration; rear = image-right end of the bed extent
measurements.reason: no calibration: the bed extent is taller than it is wide in this frame, so the side-view x-axis mapping does not apply (photo may be rotated or a top-down view)

measurements.name: load_centroid_vs_axle
measurements.method: bitmap-weighted centroid of all cargo masks along the bed axis vs the axle estimate position (midpoint of axle centres when several), scaled by the calibration
measurements.reason: no calibration: the bed extent is taller than it is wide in this frame, so the side-view x-axis mapping does not apply (photo may be rotated or a top-down view)

measurements.name: tarp_coverage
measurements.method: tarp/canvas mask area overlapping the cargo area, as a percentage of the cargo area (bitmap union on the image canvas)
measurements.reason: load type is 'steel', not loose material; the tarp check only applies to loose loads

measurements.name: tiedown_coverage_gaps
measurements.method: tie-down anchor positions mapped onto the bed axis (anchor centre x in bed coordinates); spans between neighbouring anchors and the bed ends, scaled by the calibration
measurements.reason: no tie-down detections in this detection set: tie-downs are counted from anchor close-up photos plus tap-to-correct, and close-up coordinates live in the close-up photo's own image space, so they cannot be placed on this photo's bed axis

notes: calibration unavailable: the bed extent is taller than it is wide in this frame, so the side-view x-axis mapping does not apply (photo may be rotated or a top-down view); inch measurements are reported as could_not_measure rather than guessed
load_centroid_vs_axle is a visual estimate of where the load's bulk sits; it is not a weight measurement

verdicts.finding: Forward blocking cannot be judged: there is no calibrated measurement of the load against the bed (the bed extent is taller than it is wide in this frame, so the side-view x-axis mapping does not apply (photo may be rotated or a top-down view)). Run the measurement stage with the trailer bed length to enable this check.
verdicts.confidence_basis: no calibration: the bed extent is taller than it is wide in this frame, so the side-view x-axis mapping does not apply (photo may be rotated or a top-down view)

verdicts.finding: This load needs 2 tie-down(s) for its length (10 ft), but no tie-downs could be counted: tie-downs are counted from anchor close-up photos plus any you mark by tapping them on the photo, and neither was supplied. Full-frame photos cannot count straps reliably (they are too thin to read at that distance).
verdicts.confidence_basis: no close-up detection set and no user tie-down marks supplied

verdicts.cfr_citation: 49 CFR Part 393, Subpart I (overhang; lights and plate visibility)
verdicts.finding: Overhang: could not be measured (no calibration: the bed extent is taller than it is wide in this frame, so the side-view x-axis mapping does not apply (photo may be rotated or a top-down view)). Lights and plate: the rear photo read could not tell whether both are visible.
verdicts.confidence_basis: lights/plate from the dual-model cross-check rear read (Muse Spark); SAM has no equivalent signal
verdicts.citation: 49 CFR Part 393, Subpart I (overhang; lights and plate visibility)

verdicts.cfr_citation: 49 CFR 393.100 (load placement; visual estimate only here)
verdicts.finding: Weight placement cannot be called: no calibration: the bed extent is taller than it is wide in this frame, so the side-view x-axis mapping does not apply (photo may be rotated or a top-down view). Placement is a visual estimate only in any case - a photo shows where the bulk sits, never how heavy it is.
verdicts.confidence_basis: visual estimate only; no usable centroid measurement
verdicts.citation: 49 CFR 393.100 (load placement; visual estimate only here)

verdicts.finding: Edge protection cannot be judged from the evidence supplied: it needs a close-up of each strap where it crosses an edge, read for protectors. Take an anchor close-up per tie-down and run the cross-check.
verdicts.confidence_basis: no close-up cross-check evidence about straps over edges

verdicts.finding: Tie-down strength cannot be checked from the photo: a photo cannot verify working load limit ratings or load weight, and this check needs both numbers. Missing: no tie-down working load limit ratings were supplied; no load weight was supplied. Supply the load weight and each tie-down's rating and this check runs on those numbers.
verdicts.confidence_basis: not computable: no tie-down working load limit ratings were supplied; no load weight was supplied

report.headline: More photos and details needed to judge load
report.body:
Forward blocking could not be told. Provide a correctly oriented side view for calibration.
This 10 ft load needs 2 tie-downs but none could be counted. Supply anchor close-up photos or mark tie-downs by tapping the photo.
Overhang could not be measured for the same calibration reason. Provide a side view and a clear rear photo showing lights and plate.
Weight placement could not be called for the same reason. Provide a calibrated side view.
Edge protection could not be judged. Take a close-up of each strap where it crosses an edge.
Tie-down strength could not be checked. Supply tie-down working load limit ratings and load weight.
A photo cannot verify strap tension, tie-down ratings, or load weight.
